title: Integrally closedness from a localization cocone.
statement: Let I be a small filtered category and D a diagram of commutative rings. Let c be a colimit cocone of D with point identified with a commutative ring R. If every D(i) is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field, then R is integrally closed in its fraction field.

source.place: Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma Tag 037D, common-stage lifting argument

proof.text: The colimit point is a domain by the filtered domain cocone theorem. Choose a fraction a/b representing the given integral element in its fraction field; b is nonzero.

Lift the fraction, numerator, denominator and finitely many polynomial coefficients to a common stage. Clear denominators by Polynomial.scaleRoots and use filtered-colimit equality detection to move the resulting zero relation to a later stage. Integrally closedness at that stage gives the quotient in the stage ring; mapping it to the cocone point and cancelling the nonzero denominator proves the conclusion.

statement_change.old_statement: Given a filtered cocone whose objects are the localizations at contracted primes and whose cocone point is a specified ring, if every object localization is integrally closed then the cocone point ring is integrally closed.
statement_change.what: Restore the normal-domain assumptions of Tag 037D. The common-stage Lean statement also omitted IsColimit c, so originally any cocone from Z would falsely force its point to be integrally closed. The localized conclusion is now restricted to the domain case used by the parent normal-ring theorem, whose statement is unchanged. The stronger integral-closedness-only generalization is not proved or silently reused.

old_proof.text: Lift a monic relation and its fraction to one common stage; integrally closedness at that stage puts the fraction in the stage, and the cocone map puts it in the cocone point.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $I$ be a small filtered category, $i\mapsto D_i$ a functor from $I$ to commutative rings such that every $D_i$ is an integrally closed domain, and let $R$ be a commutative ring which is the vertex of a colimit cocone over this diagram. Then $R$ is integrally closed.

proof.text:
As in the domain case, $R$ is a domain: it is nonzero (a filtered colimit of nonzero rings) and a relation $xy=0$ is realized at some stage, where it forces $x$ or $y$ to vanish. Let $z$ in the fraction field of $R$ be integral over $R$; write $z=a/b$ with $b
eq0$ and $z^n+c_1z^{n-1}+\dots+c_n=0$, i.e. $a^n+c_1a^{n-1}b+\dots+c_nb^n=0$ in $R$. By filteredness, $a,b,c_1,\dots,c_n$ lift to elements $a_i,b_i,c_{k,i}$ of one $D_i$ satisfying the same relation, and $b_i
eq0$ since $b
eq0$. Then $a_i/b_i$ is integral over $D_i$, so $a_i=d\,b_i$ for some $d\in D_i$ by integral closedness of $D_i$; mapping to $R$ gives $a= ar d\,b$, i.e. $z= ar d\in R$.
